{{Wireless adapter |brand=Netgear |model=WNDA3200 |revision= |upc=606449070989 |ean= |asin=B009XSPZ0U;GB; |price= |est_release_date=08/2010 |fcc_date= |manuf_country=China |is_manuf=No |manuf=SerComm |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |availability=UK only |if=USB |if_bus_version=2.0 |if_connector_type=Male A |form_factor=dongle |vendor_id=0846 |device_id=9018 |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |id_string= |fcc_id= |ic_id= |chip1_brand=Atheros |chip1_model=AR7010 |chip2_brand=Atheros |chip2_model=AR9280 |chip3_brand= |chip3_model= |chip4_brand= |chip4_model= |addl_chips= |accessible_UART=Yes |flags=install flash drive |ant_conn= |802dot11_protocols=abgn |txchains=2 |rxchains=2 |sstreams=2 |oui=E0:91:F5 |lin_driver= |win_driver=use included driver }} ''Wireless 11N Dual Band USB Adapter''
The device has been released ('''Virgin Media''' branded) in the UK only.
This device makes use of AR7010's mass storage mode (and an onboard 8 MB '''Macronix''' SPI Flash <small>[MX25L6445EM2I-10G]</small>) to provide automatic driver+utility installation in Windows. :For use in Linux, the mass storage device (USB ID: 0cf3:20ff) must be ejected before the actual device (USB ID: 0846:9018) is recognized.. however, any recent version of '''ath9k_htc''' should handle this.
"YTU20-RA-1.0" is silkscreened on the board in the images below. :A date code of '''1048''' (Dec. 2010) is silkscreened on the back of the board w/ the PCB manuf. info. The device's EEPROM has the regdomain set to 0x65.
{{WiFiCert|WFA9657|08/03/2010}}
